affordance_in_statement: Each element in the sequence must be chosen from the set {1, 2, 3}, and every condition requires gcd(C[u]!, C[v]!) to be strictly less than max(C[u], C[v]).
removal_suggestion: There is no semantics-preserving wording change that removes this affordance: for values 1, 2, and 3, the factorial condition is exactly C[u] != C[v]. An opaque lookup-table presentation could hide the arithmetic, but it would not defeat a graph-coloring solver.

survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The allowed values are {1, 2, 3} and the factorial inequality is equivalent to unequal endpoint values.

common_affordance: The factorial inequality collapses to C[u] != C[v], so the task is exactly deciding 3-colorability of the graph formed by the input pairs.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: It correctly recognized the factorial relation but exhaustively enumerated all 3^n sequences, causing TLE at the permitted n <= 40.

recommended_edit: No admissible edit can defeat all survivors without changing the core task: any semantics-preserving presentation still describes graph 3-coloring, and merely obscuring the factorial calculation will not affect their accepted coloring algorithms.
